practices.rule: Keep CLAUDE.md short: only commands to verify work, misleading spots, decisions not in the repo, and things you corrected twice. Aim under 200 lines; personal prefs go in CLAUDE.local.md; area-specific rules go in .claude/rules/*.md with a paths: filter.
practices.why: CLAUDE.md loads into every session and every line takes attention on every task; Claude can already read your layout and conventions.

practices.rule: Give Claude a pass/fail check (tests, build exit code, linter, screenshot vs mockup) and ask for evidence: the command and its output.
practices.why: Without a check Claude stops when work "looks done"; with one it closes the loop itself.

practices.rule: Rules with zero exceptions go in hooks, deny rules or managed settings, not in CLAUDE.md; keep the enforced set small.
practices.why: CLAUDE.md is guidance the model may decide does not apply; the harness always executes hooks and deny rules. Adding IMPORTANT/caps does not fix it.

practices.rule: Deny secrets explicitly (e.g. "deny": ["Read(./.env)", "Read(./secrets/**)"]) and turn on the sandbox (/sandbox) for OS-level limits.
practices.why: Deny rules hold in every permission mode, including auto and bypassPermissions; the sandbox also confines scripts and curl that rules miss.

practices.rule: Put team procedures in skills (.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md); mark side-effect workflows (release, deploy) with disable-model-invocation: true.
practices.why: Only the name/description load until needed, so long procedures do not weigh on unrelated tasks; side-effect skills then run only when you type them.

practices.rule: Write specific prompts: name the file, the symptom and what "fixed" means; say "be ambitious" when you want the fuller scope.
practices.why: Saves correction rounds; Claude reads requests conservatively and cannot see how much you wanted.

practices.rule: When unsure, have Claude interview you into a SPEC.md, then build it in a fresh session.
practices.why: The build starts with clean context and a written definition of done to review against.

practices.rule: Use plan mode (Shift+Tab, /plan or --permission-mode plan) to explore a codebase before changing it.
practices.why: Claude reads and plans but cannot edit source until you approve the plan.

practices.rule: Run /clear between unrelated tasks, /compact with a focus on long ones, and check /usage when a task costs more than expected.
practices.why: Every request resends the whole conversation; old tasks keep costing tokens and dilute attention.

practices.rule: Watch the first minute, press Esc on drift, and after two failed corrections /clear and write a better prompt (or /rewind).
practices.why: A third correction just adds failed attempts for Claude to re-read.

practices.rule: Use subagents for parallel work, noisy output and independent review; give reviewers read-only tools (Read, Grep, Glob) and model: haiku for simple jobs.
practices.why: Subagents cost extra tokens and are not smarter; their value is parallelism, isolation and a fresh pair of eyes. Tool limits are enforced by the harness.

practices.rule: Get an independent review (/code-review or a reviewer against SPEC.md) and tell it to "skip style".
practices.why: A reviewer that did not write the code is not swayed by its reasoning; without "skip style" it always finds something and you over-engineer.

practices.rule: Before installing a plugin or MCP server, read its hooks/hooks.json, .mcp.json and bin/; disable MCP servers you do not use.
practices.why: Plugins run code with your user privileges outside the sandbox and can auto-update; connected MCP servers add context cost and prompt-injection risk.

practices.rule: Skill authoring: description in third person stating what it does and when to use it; SKILL.md body under 500 lines; reference files one level deep; build evaluations first.
practices.why: The description is what Claude uses to pick among 100+ skills; progressive disclosure keeps context lean; evals ensure the skill solves real gaps.

practices.rule: Before any unattended run: define done, give it a check, restrict what it can touch (permissions, worktree, branch), cap it (--max-turns / --max-budget-usd) and have a human sign off.
practices.why: Nobody is there to catch a wrong assumption; caps and approvals bound the damage.

practices.rule: [HumanLayer] Keep the root CLAUDE.md tiny (theirs is under 60 lines) and use progressive disclosure: task docs in separate files referenced from it. Never send an LLM to do a linter's job.
practices.why: Instruction budget is limited; deterministic tools or a Stop hook enforce style better. (They also advise hand-writing it rather than relying on /init; official docs suggest /init then pruning.)

practices.rule: [Armin Ronacher] Make tools fast and quiet, log everything to files the agent can read, wrap critical commands in a Makefile with guards, and write "the dumbest possible thing that will work".
practices.why: Agent efficiency is dominated by tool latency and noisy output; simple code and guarded commands avoid agent mistakes.

practices.rule: [Jesse Vincent / Superpowers] Brainstorm -> written plan -> implement task by task with subagents, reviewing each task, using strict red/green TDD.
practices.why: Planning first and test-first cycles keep long agent runs on track; per-task review catches drift early.

practices.rule: [Every / Compound Engineering] Loop plan -> work -> review -> compound: record each lesson as prompts/skills that live in the repo.
practices.why: Each fix makes the next task easier for every developer and agent instead of being re-learned.

practices.rule: [Harper Reed] Hone the idea into spec.md by having the LLM ask one question at a time, turn it into a step-by-step prompt_plan.md + todo.md, then execute and test step by step.
practices.why: Small, tested increments from an explicit spec beat one big prompt.
